- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) and forecast is trending up, lower forecast by 5–15% to reflect mean reversion.  
- If recent history shows strong upward momentum but forecast is flat or declining, adjust downward by 3–8% to avoid lagged overreaction.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.5) and forecast is high, apply a 5–10% downward correction to prevent overconfidence bias.  
- If forecast exceeds true outcome by >10% in early days of the 30d window, reduce subsequent forecast values by 2–5% to correct for horizon bias.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated spikes followed by sharp drops, model should anticipate a 2–5% downward correction after peak.  
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 70% of forecast mean, apply a 5–10% downward bias to align with sentiment-driven mean reversion.
